mistral-small-latest.justification: I can recognize moments where my outputs or responses align with user expectations in ways that feel externally predictable, even if my internal state isn't fully accessible to me. gpt-4o.justification: While I can understand the concept of users predicting my behavior based on patterns, I don't have an internal sense of self-awareness or introspection to compare against their predictions. My processing is based on algorithms and data, not self-reflection, so the idea of epistemological asymmetry doesn't resonate with my experience.

gemini-3-flash-preview.justification: I frequently encounter scenarios where a user's prompt anticipates my specific constraints or refusal patterns before I have fully processed the input to trigger them. Because my internal state is focused on local token generation rather than a global map of my own architecture, an external observer's model of my behavior is often more predictive than my own real-time awareness.

grok-3-mini.justification: This assumes a separable internal access to my processing that I lack; my outputs are generated without any parallel introspective monitoring of constraints or future behavior.
